sources.title: Introduction
sources.finding: Amp offers web, macOS, iOS, Android and CLI access to threads; Orbs keep working after closing the laptop.

sources.title: Pricing
sources.locator: Amp tiers; How usage is charged; Enterprise; Notes
sources.finding: Hobby includes product features with separately billed hosted Orbs and inference routes. Teams have no additional charge; enterprise pricing is custom.

sources.title: Multiplayer
sources.finding: Workspace members can co-prompt an enabled thread and access its Orb or shared runner; access is time-limited and bills the owner.

sources.title: Modes & models
sources.finding: Task and Read Thread subagents have separate context, report summaries and support follow-up work. They cannot communicate directly with one another.

sources.title: GitHub & Git
sources.finding: A GitHub App authorizes selected repositories, branches and PRs; events can continue a thread or spawn a new Orb.

sources.title: Automations & webhooks
sources.finding: A saved thread schedule wakes the same agent and Orb; one-off, recurring and completion-conditioned runs are documented.

sources.title: MCP
sources.finding: Amp manages local and remote MCP definitions with OAuth or headers; no external-tool call was tested.

sources.title: AGENTS.md
sources.finding: Repository, personal and managed guidance has documented inclusion scopes; workspace guidance excludes subagents, Puck and raw custom agents.

sources.title: Orbs
sources.locator: Orb spawn pacing; review; follow along
sources.finding: Per-thread Orbs preserve files and services across idle pauses and queue starts beyond a documented burst allowance.

sources.title: Sizes & costs
sources.locator: Available sizes; Billing; When an Orb pauses
sources.finding: Hosted sizes and hourly rates are published and billed by minute; idle pause stops charges. Enterprise self-hosted pricing changes after November 13.

sources.title: Amp for Windows
sources.finding: Experimental Windows 10 1809+/Windows 11 app for x64 and Arm. Threads and orbs, Windows notifications and taskbar actions are documented.

sources.title: Threads
sources.finding: Changes has per-commit diffs and navigation. Thread exports are Markdown or owner-only JSON. Artifacts are editable documents with revisions, conflict detection and Markdown/HTML/PDF export.

sources.title: Shipping Changes
sources.locator: Default Ship Flow; Ship Behavior; Restack Changes
sources.finding: Default Ship commits, rebases, runs tests and pushes to the base branch. Push to Branch changes the destination; Custom Ship is a configurable prompt. Substantive conflicts require confirmation.

sources.title: Customizing Orbs
sources.finding: Project snapshots reuse dependencies up to 72 hours. Setup and resume scripts have distinct credentials and lifetimes. Services are declared separately; failed setup is visible in Setup Log.

sources.title: Self-Hosted Orbs
sources.locator: How It Works; Caution; infrastructure table
sources.finding: An outbound provider runs user-supplied spawn/pause/delete dispatch. Docker and Kubernetes examples retain disk but not memory. Self-hosted Orbs still connect to Amp.

sources.title: Runners
sources.locator: Start a Runner; Create a Worktree
sources.finding: Runners serve local or remote directories. New Worktree creates a sibling checkout and branch; threads can archive and remove only clean worktrees.

sources.title: Workspaces
sources.finding: Member uses shared resources; Admin also manages membership, billing, settings and policies and can inspect private threads. Enterprise adds narrower roles.

sources.title: Amp Security Reference
sources.locator: System Components; Data Security and Retention; Audit Logs; Assurance
sources.finding: Amp describes a cloud control plane without self-hosted deployments, GCP storage, separately controlled training, thread deletion, SOC 2 Type II and authentication audit logs.

sources.title: Amp Pricing
sources.locator: Amp Tiers; How Usage Is Charged
sources.finding: Hobby is recurring free with no included usage. BYO subscriptions/keys incur no Amp fees outside Enterprise. Megawatt costs $20/month with $20 usage and 750 a1.small Orb hours; compute and credits remain separate.

sources.title: Amp License Terms
sources.finding: Amp grants a revocable, nontransferable service license and reserves proprietary rights. This is a custom service license, not an open-source license.

sources.title: Amp linux
sources.locator: Linux app installation, local runner, tray and differences from Mac
sources.finding: Amp has a native Linux desktop app with install instructions, desktop integration and a systemd-backed local runner. It supports tray operation and launch arguments; the Linux app lacks Mac Puck windows/dictation and multiple windows.

sources.title: Amp models and subagents
sources.locator: Introduction same agent everywhere; Models and Subagents main agent, custom agents and system models
sources.finding: Amp uses its own agent across web, apps and CLI. The selected model is wrapped in Amp system prompts/tools; Task and Read Thread are Amp subagents. Custom plugin agents choose a model through amp.createAgent rather than selecting a third-party coding CLI harness.
